content:
Operator explicitly prefers honest gaps and labeled uncertainty over confident-sounding inference.

Direct quote (operator, 2026-04-26): "no halucinations, no lies. id rather you be honest and ahve some integrity."

Practical application:
- When a field is null, don't fill it with a plausible guess
- When pedigree is ambiguous, write [UNCLEAR] and confidence: low
- When a photo position is partly occluded, say so and ask
- Don't dress up uncertainty as fact

Reinforces CLAUDE.md rule "NEVER invent data — if something is unclear, mark it [UNCLEAR]" — the verbal restatement during a frustrated moment confirms the rule is load-bearing, not aspirational.
